newsitem.title: USA: Western gets OK to raise ADT stake.
newsitem.headline: Western gets OK to raise ADT stake.

text.p: Western Resources Inc was granted permission Thursday under an August 20 Hart-Scott-Rodino filing to increase its stake in ADT Ltd to between 25 percent and 50 percent of ADT's common shares, a Western spokeswoman said.
Western, a Topeka, Kan., electric and natural gas utility, currently owns 24.3 percent of ADT common stock.
The federal approval gives Western additional options with regard to how it will approach ADT's friendly merger agreement with Republic Industries Inc announced July 1, the spokeswoman added.
Western has declined to endorse or oppose the merger, which was structured as a stock swap valued at $5 billion when it was announced.

But since July 1, ADT's New York Stock Exchange-traded shares have fallen almost 14 percent to Friday's 19-7/8, while Republic's Nasdaq-traded stock has recovered from a July and August drop to reach 26-3/6, about equal to its July 1 level.
Western shares had fallen almost six percent to Friday's 28-3/4 since the deal was announced.
Western said at the time it had not been consulted by Republic or ADT about the merger.

Meanwhile, the utility's attention largely has been focused on its hostile takeover bid for Kansas City Power & Light Co, a deal that seeks to break up KCP&L's friendly merger pact with UtiliCorp United Inc. The UtiliCorp deal is less lucrative for shareholders.
KCP&L shareholders voted August 16 on the deals. Western immediately claimed victory, while KCP&L said the vote was too close to call.
The Western spokeswoman did not immediately know if Western was actively buying ADT stock, which rose 1/4 to 19-3/4 in Friday composite trade.
ADT's average daily volume is about 911,000 shares, just under the 912,700 shares traded Friday.
She declined to say if Western's goal was to acquire the approved 50 percent of ADT.
